This document contains **only Questions 1–4, 6, 10, and 11**, corresponding to the supplied script. Question 6 demonstrates 12 alternatives; the project requires students to select only one method and one criterion.

# Setup

Install packages once in the R console if needed: `install.packages(c("lmtest", "leaps", "glmnet"))`. Installation is not repeated during knitting.

```{r setup}
setwd("C:/Users/n01654025/Downloads/STA6166/Final_project")
# Import the tab-delimited data as a data frame
data <- read.delim("STA6166_final_project_data.tsv", header = TRUE, sep = "\t")
library(lmtest)
library(leaps)
library(glmnet)
```

# Question 1: Full Multiple Linear Regression

Fit all 15 predictors simultaneously. `summary()` displays the coefficient estimates, standard errors, t-statistics, p-values, and R-squared statistics.

```{r q1}
# Fit the full regression model
full_model <- lm(Y ~ ., data = data)
# Display regression results
summary(full_model)
```

# Question 2: Breusch–Pagan Test

This test assesses constant conditional error variance. The null is homoscedasticity; a small p-value suggests heteroscedasticity. Extract the statistic, p-value, and degrees of freedom.

```{r q2}
# Refit the full model, as in the original script
full_model <- lm(Y ~ ., data = data)
# Perform the Breusch-Pagan test
bp_result <- bptest(full_model)
print(bp_result)
# Extract test statistic, p-value, and degrees of freedom
bp_result$statistic
bp_result$p.value
bp_result$parameter
```

# Question 3: Shapiro–Wilk Normality Diagnostic

Apply Shapiro–Wilk to the OLS residuals. This is a descriptive diagnostic: residuals are generally dependent and have unequal variances even when the underlying regression errors are normal, so the standard p-value is not an exact test of error normality.

```{r q3}
full_model <- lm(Y ~ ., data = data)
# Extract OLS residuals
res <- residuals(full_model)
# Perform Shapiro-Wilk test
shapiro_result <- shapiro.test(res)
print(shapiro_result)
# Extract test statistic and p-value
shapiro_result$statistic
shapiro_result$p.value
```

# Question 4: Regression Diagnostic Plots

The residuals-versus-fitted plot helps assess constant variance and systematic patterns. The Q–Q plot helps assess departures from normality.

```{r q4}
full_model <- lm(Y ~ ., data = data)
# Display two plots side by side
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
# (a) Residuals versus fitted values
plot(full_model, which = 1)
# (b) Normal Q-Q plot
plot(full_model, which = 2)
# Restore plotting layout
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

# Question 6: Classical Model Selection

AIC, BIC, and Mallows' $C_p$ are **minimized**; adjusted $R^2$ is **maximized**. The `step()` function supports all three directions for AIC/BIC. `regsubsets()` supports forward and backward searches for $C_p$ and adjusted $R^2$. A custom greedy bidirectional function is defined in 6.9 and reused in 6.12.

## Shared setup

```{r q6-setup}
full_model <- lm(Y ~ ., data = data)
null_model <- lm(Y ~ 1, data = data)
N <- nrow(data)
```

## 6.1 Forward — AIC

Start with the intercept-only model and add variables. `k = 2` applies the AIC penalty. Report the selected formula and AIC value.

```{r q6-1}
forward_AIC <- step(null_model,
  scope = list(lower = formula(null_model), upper = formula(full_model)),
  direction = "forward",
  k = 2, trace = 0)
summary(forward_AIC)
formula(forward_AIC)
AIC(forward_AIC)
```

## 6.2 Backward — AIC

Start with all variables and remove variables. `k = 2` applies the AIC penalty. Report the selected formula and AIC value.

```{r q6-2}
backward_AIC <- step(full_model, direction = "backward", k = 2, trace = 0)
summary(backward_AIC)
formula(backward_AIC)
AIC(backward_AIC)
```

## 6.3 Bidirectional stepwise — AIC

Start with the intercept-only model and allow additions or removals. `k = 2` applies the AIC penalty. Report the selected formula and AIC value.

```{r q6-3}
stepwise_AIC <- step(null_model,
  scope = list(lower = formula(null_model), upper = formula(full_model)),
  direction = "both",
  k = 2, trace = 0)
summary(stepwise_AIC)
formula(stepwise_AIC)
AIC(stepwise_AIC)
```

## 6.4 Forward — BIC

Start with the intercept-only model and add variables. `k = log(N)` applies the BIC penalty. Report the selected formula and BIC value.

```{r q6-4}
forward_BIC <- step(null_model,
  scope = list(lower = formula(null_model), upper = formula(full_model)),
  direction = "forward",
  k = log(N), trace = 0)
summary(forward_BIC)
formula(forward_BIC)
BIC(forward_BIC)
```

## 6.5 Backward — BIC

Start with all variables and remove variables. `k = log(N)` applies the BIC penalty. Report the selected formula and BIC value.

```{r q6-5}
backward_BIC <- step(full_model, direction = "backward", k = log(N), trace = 0)
summary(backward_BIC)
formula(backward_BIC)
BIC(backward_BIC)
```

## 6.6 Bidirectional stepwise — BIC

Start with the intercept-only model and allow additions or removals. `k = log(N)` applies the BIC penalty. Report the selected formula and BIC value.

```{r q6-6}
stepwise_BIC <- step(null_model,
  scope = list(lower = formula(null_model), upper = formula(full_model)),
  direction = "both",
  k = log(N), trace = 0)
summary(stepwise_BIC)
formula(stepwise_BIC)
BIC(stepwise_BIC)
```

## 6.7 Forward — Mallows' $C_p$

`regsubsets()` builds a forward search path. `which.min()` finds the model size with minimum $C_p$ along that path.

```{r q6-7}
forward_Cp <- regsubsets(Y ~ ., data = data, nvmax = 15, method = "forward")
results <- summary(forward_Cp)
# Select the model with minimum Cp
best_size <- which.min(results$cp)
# Selected coefficients, Cp, and predictor names
coef(forward_Cp, id = best_size)
results$cp[best_size]
names(coef(forward_Cp, id = best_size))[-1]
```

## 6.8 Backward — Mallows' $C_p$

`regsubsets()` builds a backward search path. `which.min()` finds the model size with minimum $C_p$ along that path.

```{r q6-8}
backward_Cp <- regsubsets(Y ~ ., data = data, nvmax = 15, method = "backward")
results <- summary(backward_Cp)
# Select the model with minimum Cp
best_size <- which.min(results$cp)
# Selected coefficients, Cp, and predictor names
coef(backward_Cp, id = best_size)
results$cp[best_size]
names(coef(backward_Cp, id = best_size))[-1]
```

## 6.9 Bidirectional stepwise — Mallows' $C_p$

The following original custom function evaluates one-predictor additions and removals, moving to the best improving neighbor. It stops at a local optimum and does not guarantee the globally best subset. For $C_p$, the full-model residual variance is used as the common reference.

```{r q6-custom-function}
stepwise_custom <- function(data, criterion = "Cp") {
  predictors <- setdiff(names(data), "Y")
  N <- nrow(data)
  # Full model for estimating residual variance
  full <- lm(Y ~ ., data = data)
  sigma2_full <- sum(resid(full)^2) / df.residual(full)
  TSS <- sum((data$Y - mean(data$Y))^2)
  # Score a candidate model
  evaluate <- function(vars) {
    f <- reformulate(vars, response = "Y")
    fit <- lm(f, data = data)
    RSS <- sum(resid(fit)^2)
    p <- length(coef(fit)) # Includes intercept
    if (criterion == "Cp") {
      score <- RSS / sigma2_full - N + 2 * p
    } else if (criterion == "adjR2") {
      score <- 1 - (RSS / (N - p)) / (TSS / (N - 1))
    } else {
      stop("Criterion must be Cp or adjR2")
    }
    score
  }
  # Start with intercept-only model
  selected <- character(0)
  current_score <- evaluate(selected)
  repeat {
    remaining <- setdiff(predictors, selected)
    # Candidate additions
    add_models <- lapply(remaining, function(v) c(selected, v))
    # Candidate removals
    remove_models <- lapply(selected, function(v) setdiff(selected, v))
    candidates <- c(add_models, remove_models)
    if (length(candidates) == 0) break
    scores <- vapply(candidates, evaluate, numeric(1))
    if (criterion == "Cp") {
      best <- which.min(scores)
      improved <- scores[best] < current_score - 1e-10
    } else {
      best <- which.max(scores)
      improved <- scores[best] > current_score + 1e-10
    }
    if (!improved) break
    selected <- candidates[[best]]
    current_score <- scores[best]
  }
  final_model <- lm(reformulate(selected, response = "Y"), data = data)
  list(model = final_model, selected = selected,
       criterion_value = current_score)
}
```

```{r q6-9}
stepwise_Cp <- stepwise_custom(data = data, criterion = "Cp")
summary(stepwise_Cp$model)
formula(stepwise_Cp$model)
# Selected predictors and final Cp
stepwise_Cp$selected
stepwise_Cp$criterion_value
```

## 6.10 Forward — Adjusted $R^2$

`regsubsets()` builds a forward search path. `which.max()` chooses the model with the largest adjusted $R^2$ along that path.

```{r q6-10}
forward_adjR2 <- regsubsets(Y ~ ., data = data, nvmax = 15, method = "forward")
results <- summary(forward_adjR2)
# Choose the largest adjusted R-squared
best_size <- which.max(results$adjr2)
coef(forward_adjR2, id = best_size)
results$adjr2[best_size]
names(coef(forward_adjR2, id = best_size))[-1]
```

## 6.11 Backward — Adjusted $R^2$

`regsubsets()` builds a backward search path. `which.max()` chooses the model with the largest adjusted $R^2$ along that path.

```{r q6-11}
backward_adjR2 <- regsubsets(Y ~ ., data = data, nvmax = 15, method = "backward")
results <- summary(backward_adjR2)
# Choose the largest adjusted R-squared
best_size <- which.max(results$adjr2)
coef(backward_adjR2, id = best_size)
results$adjr2[best_size]
names(coef(backward_adjR2, id = best_size))[-1]
```

## 6.12 Bidirectional stepwise — Adjusted $R^2$

Reuse `stepwise_custom()` from 6.9, now maximizing adjusted $R^2$.

```{r q6-12}
stepwise_adjR2 <- stepwise_custom(data = data, criterion = "adjR2")
summary(stepwise_adjR2$model)
formula(stepwise_adjR2$model)
# Selected predictors and final adjusted R-squared
stepwise_adjR2$selected
stepwise_adjR2$criterion_value
```

# Question 10: Choose LASSO $\lambda$ by Cross-Validation

`glmnet` uses a numeric predictor matrix. With `alpha = 1`, the model is LASSO; `nfolds = 10` specifies ten-fold cross-validation, and `type.measure = "mse"` evaluates mean squared error. The seed makes the fold allocation reproducible.

## Step 1. Prepare the data

```{r q10-prepare}
# Predictor matrix: X1 through X15
X <- as.matrix(data[, paste0("X", 1:15)])
# Response vector
Y <- data$Y
# Check dimensions
dim(X)
length(Y)
```

## Step 2. Run 10-fold cross-validation

```{r q10-cv}
set.seed(6166)
cv_lasso <- cv.glmnet(x = X, y = Y, alpha = 1,
  nfolds = 10, family = "gaussian", type.measure = "mse",
  standardize = TRUE)
# Display cross-validation results
print(cv_lasso)
```

## Step 3. Plot cross-validation MSE

`plot()` shows the cross-validation error curve. A second call saves the plot to a PDF in the working directory.

```{r q10-plot}
# Plot cross-validation MSE against lambda
plot(cv_lasso)
# Save plot as PDF
pdf("Question10_LASSO_CV.pdf", width = 8, height = 6)
plot(cv_lasso)
dev.off()
```

## Step 4. Report `lambda.min`

`lambda.min` is the penalty value giving the smallest cross-validation mean squared error.

```{r q10-lambda}
lambda_selected <- cv_lasso$lambda.min
lambda_selected
# Minimum cross-validation MSE
min(cv_lasso$cvm)
```

# Question 11: Fit LASSO and Identify Variables

Fit the LASSO model using the previously chosen `lambda.min`. Extract its coefficients and identify predictors with nonzero estimates; do not count the intercept.

## Step 1. Fit LASSO using the selected $\lambda$

```{r q11-fit}
lasso_model <- glmnet(x = X, y = Y, alpha = 1,
  lambda = lambda_selected, family = "gaussian",
  standardize = TRUE)
# Display fitted model
print(lasso_model)
```

## Step 2. Extract the LASSO coefficient estimates

```{r q11-coef}
# Extract LASSO coefficients
lasso_coef <- coef(lasso_model)
print(lasso_coef)
# Convert sparse coefficients into a data frame
lasso_coef_df <- data.frame(
  Coefficient = rownames(lasso_coef),
  Estimate = as.numeric(lasso_coef)
)
print(lasso_coef_df)
```

## Step 3. Identify selected predictors

```{r q11-selected}
# Exclude intercept
beta_lasso <- lasso_coef_df[-1, ]
# Identify predictors with nonzero coefficients
selected_predictors <- beta_lasso$Coefficient[
  beta_lasso$Estimate != 0
]
print(selected_predictors)
# Number of selected predictors
length(selected_predictors)
```

## Step 4. Create and save the coefficient table

Create a 15-row table for $\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_{15}$; a zero estimate means LASSO did not select that predictor. Save a CSV that students can copy into their report.

```{r q11-table}
lasso_table <- data.frame(
  Coefficient = paste0("beta", 1:15),
  LASSO_Point_Estimate = as.numeric(
    lasso_coef[paste0("X", 1:15), 1]
  )
)
print(lasso_table)
# Optional: save as CSV
write.csv(lasso_table, "Question11_LASSO_Coefficients.csv",
          row.names = FALSE)
```
